components.explanation: The map generator's TIER, RAMP_RUN, RAMP_APRON and corridor half-width set every asset size; TerrainSurface already builds each ramp's slope and each cliff's face and collision, so the assets are dressing over it.
cliff_wall_segment: three cube strata and one icosphere built by eight verbatim MCP calls; call 6 fixed the buried lip boulder found by look. 116 triangles, origin at the bottom of the face line.
cliff_rubble_pile: three flattened icospheres; call 5 sank the floating top stone found by look. 180 triangles.

arched_ramp_segment: a plane edited into a cambered wedge by top_z, plus two kerbs; the author moved both kerbs 0.1 m outward by hand, and a read-only MCP call verified it. 68 triangles, 18.7 degrees.
export_glb.py exports each .blend headless as +Y-up glTF binary (Blender +Y becomes Godot -Z); .gdignore keeps Godot from importing .blend files and the write-up; *.blend1 backups are ignored.
asset_preview.tscn: ground, sun, the game's camera and a 1.7 m capsule beside the three assets; its sun basis was first written by columns and lit the scene from below.
test_a3_assets.gd reads the imported meshes back (bounds, node transforms, triangles, colours, ramp direction and slope); capture_a3_preview.gd renders the preview scene to PNG.

excerpts.text:
const TIER := 2.2
const MAX_TIER := 2
## Horizontal run one tier of ramp needs: 2.2 over 6.5 is ~19°, well inside
## the navmesh's 35° and the character's 45°.
const RAMP_RUN := 6.5
const RAMP_APRON := 2.0

# --- call 6 ---
# Step 4b (fix after look): the boulder was buried 0.2 of its 0.35 in strata_top and read as a disc.
# Make it 0.8 x 0.6 x 0.5 and set it on the front lip so it bulges out of the face:
# z 1.9-2.4 (peak still 2.4), front at y = -0.30 (the brief's front limit).
import bpy
obj = bpy.data.objects["lip_boulder"]
d = obj.dimensions.copy()
obj.scale = (0.80 / d.x, 0.60 / d.y, 0.50 / d.z)
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
obj.select_set(True)
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=True, scale=True)
obj.location = (0.75, 0.0, 2.40 - 0.25)

RISE, RUN, HALF_W, CROWN, TAPER, CLEAR = 2.2, 6.5, 3.4, 0.10, 0.5, 0.02

def top_z(x, y):
    taper = max(0.0, min(1.0, min(y, RUN - y) / TAPER))
    return RISE * y / RUN + CLEAR + CROWN * (1.0 - abs(x) / HALF_W) * taper

# --- manual edit by the author (not code) ---
# 2026-10-12: the author opened this file in Blender and, by hand in Edit Mode,
# selected each kerb (L) and moved it outward along X by 0.1 m (G X 0.1 / G X -0.1),
# then saved (Ctrl+S). Overall width 6.8 -> 7.0. Reason: bury the kerb's outer edge
# 0.1 into the corridor's rock bank so the seam is covered.

bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(
    filepath=out,
    export_format="GLB",
    use_selection=True,
    export_yup=True,
    export_apply=True,
    export_cameras=False,
    export_lights=False,
    export_materials="EXPORT",
)

# F1: the high end must be at -Z. F4: the edge slope must stay under 19 deg.
		var high_z := 0.0
		var top_y := -1.0
		for p in points:
			if p.y > top_y - 0.001:
				if p.y > top_y + 0.001: high_z = p.z
				top_y = maxf(top_y, p.y)
		check("ramp: highest vertices at z %.2f (high end towards -Z)" % high_z, high_z < -6.0)
